I will keep to the wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is the system I know best, it fits the land and water conditions, and at my age I would rather plant crops I understand well and can manage on time. At the start of the growing season, my winter wheat is already the main crop in the field, and after harvest I will plant summer maize right away. I will not spread myself across many crops, because that makes field work, irrigation, fertilizer use, and pest control harder to manage. I will use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize because I want stable emergence, steady yield, and less risk. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage for wheat ground preparation when needed and rotary tillage again after wheat harvest so I can plant maize quickly. I will apply moderate fertilizer, not too little and not too much, because I want yield but I also need to control costs. I will irrigate wheat more times than maize, since wheat in my area usually needs more water support, while summer maize can use rainfall if the season is normal. I will spray only as needed for common diseases, insects, and weeds, because I want to protect the crop without wasting money.
